summary: Intermittent 5xx spike caused by session-affinity oscillation between edge proxies leading to runtime ejections
description:
Issue summary: Starting ~2026-03-13 02:10 UTC we observed an abrupt elevation in 5xx responses for a subset of LexiDocs routes. Impact: ~8% of their requests returned 502/503/504 over a 40-minute window; real-time dashboards reported increased tail latency and error rate alerts. Environment: prod-us-east, dedicated tenant pool for LexiDocs, serving-runtime pinned to redwood/7b-chat-v1.

Observed behavior: The api-gateway showed rapid connection churn to the edge-proxy pool backing the tenant. Edge metrics show session-affinity flips (client connections rebalanced between proxy instances on sub-second timescales). Upstream serving runtimes began ejecting workers with messages indicating half-open socket counts and keepalive mismatches; subsequent GPU worker restarts corresponded with elevated 5xx floors.

Steps to reproduce (approx from customer repro): 1) Replay a steady stream of short chat requests (payloads ~1-2 KB) at ~250 rps to the LexiDocs tenant route. 2) Force a route shift by toggling a dummy weight on the edge balancer to simulate minor topology change. 3) Observe keepalive reuse counters on the edge proxy and watch for affinity TTL refreshes.

Initial hypothesis: A race between the edge-proxy affinity TTL refresh and the api-gateway's connection reuse optimization leads to alternating TCP handoffs; this produces half-closed sockets and a burst of upstream accept/close events. The serving-runtime's socket accounting then triggers worker ejections (safety ladder), causing transient GPU worker restarts and a higher 5xx floor.

Immediate mitigations applied: - Pinned LexiDocs traffic to a single stable edge-proxy pool for the tenant (manual routing override). - Temporarily disabled aggressive connection reuse on the api-gateway for the tenant route. - Increased runtime worker socket soft-limit to reduce premature ejections while we investigate.

Next steps: Continue root-cause analysis of affinity refresh logic and connection reuse interplay; implement a canary fix to smooth affinity refresh windows and add defensive keepalive validation in the proxy.

investigation_notes: 2026-03-13 02:40 UTC - Captured tcpdump from edge-proxy-03: repeated FIN/ACK sequences where client connection appeared to be reused by a different proxy instance within the affinity window.
2026-03-13 03:00 UTC - Runtime logs: worker-eject events reference 'socket_count_threshold' shortly after affinity flips; GPU restart traces align with worker process exit codes 137 and 9.
2026-03-13 04:15 UTC - Metrics: keepalive_reuse_rate spiked from 72% to 96% for the tenant; affinity_reassignments per second jumped to 14/s (baseline <1/s).
2026-03-13 04:50 UTC - Hypothesis validated in staging via synthetic replay: toggling affinity TTL from 30s->2s while enabling reuse optimization reproduces elevated worker-eject counts and 5xx wave.
2026-03-14 08:00 UTC - Determined two contributing factors: (1) affinity TTL jitter from health-check timing, (2) optimistic connection reuse logic that assumes long-lived pinning.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-14 13:50 UTC - Deployed edge-proxy canary (https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/9182) that: (a) staggers affinity refreshes to avoid synchronized flips, (b) validates keepalive ownership before reuse.
2026-03-14 14:00 UTC - Re-enabled api-gateway connection reuse with conservative time-window for the tenant; monitoring shows stable keepalive metrics and no worker ejections for 2 hours post-deploy.
2026-03-14 14:20 UTC - Informed customer with rollback plan and ETA for full rollout. Marked incident for postmortem and long-term follow-up (INT-7732).
